  • Italy's ​government will dispatch 500 army troops to "defend Milan" after two days of unrest that saw demonstrators ‌clash with police, loot shops and vandalise property, Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini said on Monday.

  • 3M lifted its 2026 profit forecast on Tuesday, a day after its expanded data-center partnership with Amazon signaled a growing focus on AI-linked offerings, sending the industrial conglomerate's shares up nearly 5%.

  • Britain's FTSE 100 ended lower on Tuesday as banks and commodity-linked stocks weighed, while signs of resilience in the labour market ​kept expectations alive for a Bank of England rate hike next ‌month.

  • Index provider MSCI has warned it might strip Indonesia of its emerging markets status next year and move it to a standalone classification, a move ​that would directly affect nine companies that are part of related indexes.

  • Britain's ‌competition regulator said on Tuesday it was seeking to loosen Apple's grip on contactless payments by proposing that the company lower fees and remove technical barriers, helping rival services compete with Apple Pay.

  • Vinted, an app for buying and selling second-hand clothing, said on Monday it had increased checks on suspicious listings and removed adverts linked to looted goods following unrest ​in France.

  • LegalcategoryOctober 19, 2026

    US grocery chain Albertsons Companies will begin making its case in court on Monday for more than $8 billion in damages against ​larger rival Kroger for allegedly sinking their agreed $24.6 billion merger two years ago.

  • Indian tax officials are ​investigating whether liquor giants Pernod Ricard and Diageo wrongly classified some bulk Scotch imports, allowing them to pay lower ‌tariffs introduced under the recently agreed India-UK trade pact, five industry sources familiar with the matter said.
